result_text:
Tickets now carry an assigned support agent, and every listed query returns it. The full offline suite passes (608 tests, BUILD SUCCESS). Nothing is committed.

The repo has no support-agent entity, so I stored the agent as a free-text name. That is a design choice you may want to revisit.

- **`schema.sql`**: `support_ticket` gets a nullable `agent VARCHAR(100)` column.
- **`model/SupportTicket.java`**: new last component `String agent`. The old 9-argument constructor remains as a secondary constructor that sets `agent` to null, so existing callers compile unchanged.
- **`DataStore.java`**: the insert writes `agent`. Every support-ticket select (customer, priority, region, sales rep, order, high-priority by region, open on date, product, and lookup by number) selects and maps it. Status updates don't touch the column, so the agent survives in-progress and close.
- **`service/SupportTicketService.java`**: new overload `create(..., date, agent)`. The existing 6-argument `create` delegates with null. A blank agent is stored as unassigned, and a name is trimmed. `changeStatus` carries the agent over.
- **`SupportTicketTest.java`**: new `assignedAgentIsKeptWhenStatusChanges` test. It covers assignment on create, an unassigned ticket, and the agent surviving in-progress and close, in the customer list and in the lookup by number.

I did not add a way to reassign a ticket, and the demo scenario still creates tickets without an agent. Say if you want either.
